mainTopic: Onion dangers, then the minimum amounts of beer, dates, and other foods needed for an עירוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing a health warning about onion leaves. They are dangerous only before the plant grows a זרת, and רב פפא says drinking beer afterward removes the danger. A ברייתא warns against eating onion because of its poison, and tells how רבי חנינא nearly died from it. The גמרא then brings שמואל's rule that beer may be used for an עירוב and that three לוגין of it invalidate a מקוה. It defends that rule against רב כהנא's objection that it is obvious from dye-water. Next it discusses the minimum amounts of different foods for an עירוב. רב אחא's proposal for beer, built on a ratio of four from the laws of carrying, is rejected. רב יוסף's proof that a קב of dates is enough is pushed back by אביי. Amounts are given for שתיתא and roasted grain, along with two health tips from אביי's foster mother. Finally, שמואל divides foods into relish and main food. רבה and רב יוסף argue about roasted meat, and אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof from the Persians, since הלכה follows the practice of most of the world.

steps.title: Onion leaves are dangerous only before the onion grows a span
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the qualification of the danger of onion leaves on the previous amud. The danger applies only before the plant has grown a זרת (a span).
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only where it has not yet grown a span. But if it has grown a span, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is limiting the warning about eating onion leaves, which began on the previous amud. The leaves are only dangerous while the plant is still young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement warned that onion leaves are harmful. Here the warning is narrowed to leaves of a plant that has not yet reached a זרת, the stage when they are most harmful. Once the plant passes that size, there is no concern.

keyTerms.meaning: A span: the distance from the thumb to the little finger of a spread hand
We have no problem with it

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence that began on the previous amud. It is a limit on an earlier health warning about onion leaves, not a new topic.

phrases.english: where it has not grown to a span,
phrases.notes: This finishes the 'we only said this when...' limit that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: but if it has grown to a span —
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא אִבְּצִיל זִירְתָּא, אֲבָל אִבְּצִיל זִירְתָּא לֵית לַן בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the onion-leaf warning earlier and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger of onion leaves applies only before the plant reaches the size of a זרת.

steps.title: Drinking beer afterward removes the danger
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds a second limit: the danger applies only if the person did not drink beer afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We only said this where he did not drink beer. But if he drank beer, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows the warning even further. Beer cancels out the harm of the onion leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 limited the danger based on the age of the plant. רב פפא adds a limit based on what the person does afterward. If he drinks שכר, the harmful effect is neutralized.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when…: a formula that limits an earlier statement
Beer (usually made from dates or barley in Bavel)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We only said this
where he did not drink beer,
but if he drank beer,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to the same onion-leaf warning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one drinks beer after eating onion leaves, there is no danger.

steps.title: A ברייתא warns not to eat onion because of its poison
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person should not eat onion because of the poison (נחש) inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person should not eat onion, because of the poison that is in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a general warning against eating onion. The story that follows backs it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נחש here does not mean an actual snake. It means a harmful, toxic substance in the onion. This continues the theme of the danger of onions.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the snake in it': the poison or toxin in the onion

steps.confusionAlert: נחש here is not a real snake. It is a way of describing the poison in the onion.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person should not eat onion,
because of the poison that is in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם בָּצָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same health topic of onion danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not eat onion because of its toxin.

steps.title: The story of רבי חנינא, who nearly died from onion
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא ate half an onion with its poison and became deathly ill. He recovered only through the prayers of his colleagues, because his generation needed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident with רבי חנינא. He ate half an onion and half of its poison, became ill, and was close to dying. His colleagues prayed for mercy for him, and he lived, because the time needed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story that proves how dangerous onion poison is. A great sage almost died from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the danger is real. רבי חנינא survived only because of the prayers of his colleagues and because his generation needed his teaching. Without that, he would not have recovered.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident / story brought as support
The time needed him: his generation needed him

steps.whatToRemember: Onion and especially onion leaves can be dangerous. The danger is limited to a young plant (before it grows a זרת) and is removed by drinking beer. The story of רבי חנינא shows how serious it is.

phrases.english: And there was an incident with Rabbi Ḥanina
who ate half an onion
and half of the poison in it,
and he became ill and was close to dying,
and his colleagues prayed for mercy for him
and he lived,
because the time needed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story that supports the ברייתא's warning.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's warning that onion poison is dangerous.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident in which רבי חנינא nearly died after eating half an onion.

steps.title: שמואל: beer works for an עירוב and invalidates a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes שמואל with two rules about beer. It may be used for an עירוב, and three לוגין of it invalidate a מקוה, just like drawn water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of שמואל: One may make an עירוב with beer, and it invalidates a מקוה with three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the health discussion back to הלכה. It brings שמואל's two rulings about beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beer counts as food, so it can be used for an עירוב, unlike plain water. For a מקוה, three לוגין of drawn water (מים שאובין) invalidate it. שמואל teaches that beer is treated the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: One may make an עירוב with it
Three לוגין: the amount of drawn water that invalidates a מקוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: why would שמואל need to teach the מקוה rule if it seems obvious?

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Shmuel said:
One may establish an eiruv with beer,
and it invalidates a ritual bath
with three log.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: שֵׁכָר מְעָרְבִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the onion topic and opens a new halachic topic: beer. The link is that beer was just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beer is valid for an עירוב, and three לוגין of beer invalidate a מקוה, like drawn water.

steps.title: רב כהנא objects: this is obvious, just like dye-water
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא objects to שמואל's ruling about the מקוה. He says it is obvious, since it is no different from dye-water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא challenged it: This is obvious! What is the difference between this and dye-water?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges שמואל's מקוה rule as unnecessary. The next step brings the source he relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא does not dispute the ruling itself. He argues that it teaches nothing new: if colored water like dye-water invalidates a מקוה, beer should obviously do the same.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious: a challenge that a statement adds nothing new

steps.confusionAlert: A פשיטא challenge does not claim the ruling is wrong. It only asks why it needed to be said.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana strongly objects to this:
It is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה לְמֵי צֶבַע?
phrases.english: For what is the difference between this and dye-water?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second half of שמואל's statement as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that beer invalidates a מקוה with three לוגין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If dye-water, which is changed water, already invalidates a מקוה with three לוגין, beer should obviously do the same. So the ruling adds nothing new.

steps.title: The משנה: רבי יוסי says dye-water invalidates a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא cites a משנה in which רבי יוסי rules that three לוגין of dye-water invalidate a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יוסי says: Dye-water invalidates a מקוה with three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: This step gives the source behind רב כהנא's challenge. A משנה already teaches the dye-water rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dye-water has been changed by the dye, yet רבי יוסי still treats it like drawn water. רב כהנא uses this to argue that beer is the same and needed no new teaching.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Rabbi Yosei says:
Dye-water invalidates a ritual bath
with three log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב כהנא's פשיטא challenge.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's claim that שמואל's מקוה ruling is obvious.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in which רבי יוסי rules that three לוגין of dye-water invalidate a מקוה.

steps.title: Beer has its own name, so the ruling is a real חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that dye-water is still called 'water', while beer is called by its own name. So we might have thought beer is not water at all, and שמואל's teaching was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: There, it is called 'dye-water'. Here, it is called 'beer'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל and shows that his ruling teaches something new. The difference is the name of the liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dye-water still carries the name 'water', so it is easy to treat it like drawn water. Beer has a totally different name, so one might think it is not water at all. In that case it would only invalidate a מקוה if it changed the water's color. שמואל teaches that beer still counts like drawn water.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here: a formula that contrasts two cases

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: beer is valid for an עירוב, and three לוגין of it invalidate a מקוה. This is not obvious from dye-water, because beer has its own name and we might have thought it is not water at all.

phrases.english: They said:
There, it is called 'dye-water';
here, it is called 'beer'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם מַיָּא דְצִבְעָא מִיקְּרֵי, הָכָא שִׁיכְרָא אִיקְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's פשיטא challenge by pointing to a real difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): the name of the liquid makes beer different from dye-water.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since beer has its own name and is not called water, one might think it is not water at all. Then it would invalidate a מקוה only by changing the water's color.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל teaches that beer, despite its separate name, invalidates a מקוה with three לוגין, like drawn water.

steps.title: How much beer is needed for an עירוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what minimum amount of beer is needed to make an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with how much beer do we make an עירוב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now knows from שמואל that beer may be used for an עירוב, so it asks how much is needed. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 told us beer is allowed, but it did not give an amount. An עירוב needs enough food for two meals, so we need to know how much beer counts as two meals.

keyTerms.meaning: With how much? What is the amount?

phrases.english: And with how much (beer) do we make an eruv?
phrases.notes: Continues from שמואל's rule that beer may be used for an עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to שמואל's first rule (beer for an עירוב) after the side discussion about the מקוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of beer needed for an עירוב.

steps.title: רב אחא proposes two quarters of a קב of beer
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף suggests to his father רב יוסף that the amount is two quarters of a קב of beer, which is two לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רב יוסף, wanted to say in front of רב יוסף: with two quarters (of a קב) of beer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא offers an answer: two quarters of a קב of beer, which equals two לוגין. The word 'סבר' warns us that this is only his proposal, and it may be rejected later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two quarters of a קב is a large amount. It is four times the two רביעיות of wine needed for an עירוב. The next steps explain where this ratio of four comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say. This shows a proposal that may be rejected.

steps.confusionAlert: 'סבר' does not mean this is the final law. It signals a suggestion, and the גמרא is about to reject it.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Yosef, thought
phrases.notes: The word סבר, 'thought,' is a hint that this idea might not hold up.

phrases.english: to say before Rav Yosef:
with two quarters (of a kav) of beer,
phrases.notes: Two quarters of a קב is two לוגין, four times the wine amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two quarters of a קב of beer, which is two לוגין.

steps.title: Wine for carrying is only a quarter of a רביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא starts his proof. You are liable for carrying out wine if you carry enough for a cup of blessing. That is a quarter of a רביעית, because good wine is mixed with three parts water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: one who carries out wine on שבת is liable for enough to mix a cup. A ברייתא adds: enough to mix a fine cup. What is a fine cup? A כוס של ברכה. And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: a כוס של ברכה needs a quarter of a רביעית of wine, so that after mixing it with water it reaches a full רביעית. This fits רבא's rule: any wine that cannot take three parts water to one part wine is not real wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא begins building his proof. He first shows that the amount of wine for liability when carrying on שבת is very small: only a quarter of a רביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain works like this. You are liable for enough wine to make a fine cup, and a fine cup is a כוס של ברכה. That cup must hold a full רביעית after mixing. Since real wine takes three parts water for every one part wine, you only need a quarter of a רביעית of plain wine.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out (from a private to a public domain on שבת)
Mixing a cup (diluting wine with water)
A cup of blessing (for ברכת המזון, קידוש, etc.)

phrases.english: As we learned: one who carries out wine,
(is liable for) enough to mix a cup.

phrases.aramaic: וְתָנֵי עֲלַהּ: כְּדֵי מְזִיגַת כּוֹס יָפֶה.
phrases.english: And it was taught about it: enough to mix a fine cup.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי כּוֹס יָפֶה? כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה.
phrases.english: What is a fine cup? A cup of blessing.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ רוֹבַע רְבִיעִית,
phrases.english: A cup of blessing must contain a quarter of a revi'it,
so that one mixes it and it comes to a full revi'it.
And this follows Rava, for Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל חַמְרָא דְּלָא דָּרֵי עַל חַד תְּלָת מַיָּא —
phrases.english: Any wine that cannot carry three parts water to one —
is not (proper) wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the source for רב אחא's proposal.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחא's claim that the beer amount is four times the wine amount.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about carrying on שבת, a ברייתא, רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה, and רבא's rule about mixing wine.

steps.title: Other drinks need four times as much, so beer should too
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה says other drinks need a full רביעית. That is four times the wine amount, so רב אחא applies the same ratio of four to beer for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the end of the משנה teaches: all other drinks are a רביעית, and all waste water is a רביעית. Since there the ratio is one to four, here too the ratio is one to four.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא finishes his proof. For carrying, other drinks need four times the wine amount, so he says beer needs four times the wine amount for an עירוב as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine for carrying is a quarter of a רביעית, while other drinks are a full רביעית, so the ratio is one to four. An עירוב with wine takes two רביעיות. Four times that is eight רביעיות, which is two לוגין, or two quarters of a קב.

keyTerms.meaning: The end clause of a משנה

phrases.english: And the latter clause teaches:
and all other liquids, with a revi'it,
and all waste water, with a revi'it.
Since there it is one to four —
phrases.notes: For carrying, the amount for wine is a quarter רביעית, but other drinks need a full רביעית.

phrases.english: here too (for eruv) it is one to four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 11 by drawing the ratio of four.
steps.raayaObject: The two-לוגין amount of beer for an עירוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end clause of the משנה about carrying liquids on שבת.

steps.title: The ratio from carrying does not apply to an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אחא. For carrying, a small amount of beer is simply not worth anything. For an עירוב, the question is food, and people are satisfied by one cup of beer in the morning and one in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There (for carrying), less than that amount is not considered important. But here (for an עירוב), that is not the case, because people often drink a cup in the morning and a cup in the evening and rely on them as their meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב אחא's comparison. It explains that carrying and עירוב measure different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For carrying, the question is whether the amount is significant enough to matter. Less than a רביעית of beer is not. For an עירוב, the question is whether the amount works as two meals. One cup of beer in the morning and one in the evening already fill people up, so there is no reason to require four times the wine amount.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so (a rejection)

steps.whatToRemember: The amount for carrying on שבת depends on what is significant. The amount for an עירוב depends on what fills a person as a meal. So the ratio of four from carrying does not carry over to beer for an עירוב.

phrases.english: But it is not so,

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דִּבְצִיר מֵהֲכִי לָא חֲשִׁיב,
phrases.english: there it is that less than this is not significant,
but here — not so.
For people commonly drink a cup in the morning
and a cup in the evening, and rely on them (as meals).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison built in steps 11 and 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects carrying over the ratio of four from carrying to an עירוב, and with it the two-לוגין amount.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Carrying measures significance, while an עירוב measures a satisfying meal. A small amount of beer counts as a meal.

steps.title: How many dates are needed for an עירוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks what amount of dates is needed for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Dates — with how much (do we make an עירוב)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new food and asks how many dates are needed. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same question we asked about beer is now asked about dates. Each food fills a person differently, so each needs its own amount.

phrases.english: Dates — with how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about a different food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of dates for an עירוב.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a קב of dates
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a קב of dates is needed for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: dates, with a קב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question: a קב of dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a fixed amount for dates. In the next step רב יוסף shows where he learned it.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of volume, equal to four לוגין

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: dates, with a kav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.

steps.title: רב יוסף's source: paying back figs with dates
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא. Someone ate dried figs of תרומה and paid back with dates, and a blessing comes on him. This shows dates are a better food than figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: from where do I say this? As it was taught: if someone ate dried figs (of תרומה) and paid back with dates, may a blessing come upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the source for his ruling. A person who pays back figs with dates deserves a blessing, so dates must be worth more than figs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person only earns a blessing for paying back something better than what he took. So dates are a better, more filling food than dried figs. That means the amount of dates for an עירוב does not need to be larger than the amount for figs.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
May a blessing come upon him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught: if he ate dried figs and paid back dates —
phrases.notes: The case is a person who ate תרומה by mistake and must pay it back.

phrases.english: may a blessing come upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's ruling in step 15.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about paying back תרומה figs with dates.

steps.title: How exactly does the case work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case of the ברייתא about paying back figs with dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask how the ברייתא's case works. This sets up the next move, where it tests two ways to read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof only works if we know how the payback was measured. The question opens two options: payment by value or payment by amount.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ברייתא quoted by רב יוסף actually works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was the payback measured by value or by amount?

steps.title: Paying by value would not earn a blessing
steps.stepSummary: If he paid a זוז of dates for a זוז of figs, nothing special happened, so why a blessing?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he paid according to value, meaning he ate a זוז worth and paid a זוז worth, why does it say 'a blessing comes on him'? He ate a זוז and paid a זוז!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading, that he paid by value, and shows it does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An even trade of one זוז for one זוז gives the כהן nothing extra. So the words 'a blessing comes on him' would have no reason. This rules out the value reading, at least for now.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the first option being tested)
May a blessing come upon him

phrases.english: If you say according to value,
that he ate from it a zuz's worth
and pays him back a zuz's worth,
what is 'may a blessing come upon him'?
He ate a zuz's worth, he pays a zuz's worth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question and finds a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as payment by value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An even trade gives no benefit, so the blessing would have no reason.

steps.title: Paying by amount shows dates are better
steps.stepSummary: He paid a סאה of dates (worth four) for a סאה of figs (worth one), so dates are the better food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it by measure? He ate a סאה of dried figs worth one זוז and paid a סאה of dates worth four, and it says 'a blessing comes on him.' So dates are better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the other reading, payment by amount, and uses it to finish רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same amount, but the dates are worth four times as much, so the כהן clearly gains. That is the blessing. Since dates are better than figs, and a קב of figs works for an עירוב, a קב of dates surely works too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (pushing to the other option)
A סאה, a measure of volume

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core of רב יוסף's support for using a קב of dates for an עירוב.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not according to measure,
that he ate from it a se'a of dried figs
worth one zuz,
and pays him back a se'a of dates
worth four (zuz),
and it teaches: 'may a blessing come upon him.'
Apparently, dates are superior.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having rejected the value reading, it accepts the measure reading and completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: Dates are a better food than dried figs, so a קב of dates is enough for an עירוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about paying back תרומה figs with dates.

steps.title: אביי: he really paid by value
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof and says the case may be payment by value after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, he ate a זוז worth and paid a זוז worth.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof. He returns to the reading that was just thrown out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is payment by value, nothing shows that dates are better per amount. So the proof falls. In the next step אביי explains why there is still a blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (going back to the first option)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Actually, he ate from it a zuz's worth,
and pays back a zuz's worth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof by reviving the value reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not necessarily רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as payment by value, so it says nothing about dates being better per amount.

steps.title: The blessing is that dates sell easily
steps.stepSummary: Even at equal value, the כהן gains, because buyers want dates and not dried figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why 'a blessing comes on him'? Because he ate something buyers don't jump at, and paid with something buyers do jump at.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the problem from step 18. He explains the blessing even in an even-value trade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing is not about getting more money. It is about getting something easier to sell. Dates move fast in the market, so the כהן is better off.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof: the ברייתא may mean equal value, and the blessing is that dates are easier to sell. So it does not prove dates are a better food.

phrases.english: And what is 'may a blessing come upon him'?
That he ate from him something
that a buyer does not jump at,
and pays him back something
that a buyer jumps at.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's rejection by answering the problem raised in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An even-value trade gives no benefit, so a blessing makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dates are easier to sell, which is the blessing, even at equal value.

steps.title: The amount of שתיתא for an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר פנחס says two big spoonfuls of שתיתא are enough for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: שתיתא: רב אחא בר פנחס said two large spoonfuls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new food and gives its amount for an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שתיתא is a filling dish of roasted flour and honey. So a small amount, two big spoonfuls, counts as two meals.

keyTerms.meaning: A dish of roasted flour mixed with honey

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתִיתָא — אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר פִּנְחָס:
phrases.english: Shetita — Rav Aḥa bar Pineḥas said:
Two large spoonfuls.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתִיתָא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר פִּנְחָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the dates discussion and gives the עירוב amount for another food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two large spoonfuls of שתיתא are enough for an עירוב.

steps.title: The amount of roasted grain for an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי says two בוני of פומבדיתא of roasted grain are enough for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: כיסאני: אביי said two בוני of פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the עירוב amount for one more food, roasted grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure is a local unit used in פומבדיתא, called a בונא. Two of them are enough for the two meals of an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Babylonian city and yeshiva

phrases.english: Kisanei — Abaye said:
Two Pumbeditan bunei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of עירוב amounts with another food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two בוני of פומבדיתא of roasted grain are enough for an עירוב.

steps.title: אביי's mother: roasted grain is good for the heart
steps.stepSummary: A side remark: אביי's foster mother told him roasted grain is good for the heart and clears away worries.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Mother told me, this roasted grain is good for the heart and drives away worrying thoughts.
steps.whatsHappening: Since roasted grain was just mentioned, the גמרא adds a side health tip from אביי's foster mother. It is not part of the עירוב law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side comment brought only because the food came up. It adds nothing to the עירוב rules. It is practical health advice אביי often quotes from his foster mother.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי's 'mother' here is his foster mother who raised him. His birth mother died when he was born.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Mother told me:
These roasted grains are good for the heart,
and drive away (worrisome) thoughts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side remark triggered by the mention of roasted grain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasted grain is good for the heart and eases worry (health advice, not law).

steps.title: A remedy for a weak heart from אביי's mother
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports another remedy from his foster mother. For heart weakness, roast the right thigh of a ram over a fire of dried cattle dung from ניסן, or willow twigs if there is no dung. Then eat it and drink diluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: Mother told me: Someone who has a weak heart should take meat from the right thigh of a ram. He should also take dried dung of grazing cattle from the month of ניסן. If there is no such dung, he should take willow twigs. He should roast the meat over that fire, eat it, and afterward drink diluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still on the side topic from step 24 and records one more health tip that אביי heard from his foster mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the עירוב discussion. Once the גמרא mentioned his mother's advice about roasted grain, it added another of her remedies. The logic of the עירוב sugya is paused here.

keyTerms.meaning: the right thigh of a ram
dried dung of grazing cattle, used as fuel

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a law about עירוב. It is a medical side remark. The עירוב discussion picks up again in the next step.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: Mother told me:
phrases.notes: This refers to his foster mother, who raised him.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ חוּלְשָׁא דְּלִיבָּא,
phrases.english: One who has weakness of the heart,
should bring meat of the right thigh of a ram,
and bring dung of grazing cattle from Nisan,
phrases.notes: The dung is used as fuel for the roasting fire.

phrases.english: and if there is no dung of grazing cattle —
he should bring willow twigs,
and roast it and eat,
and drink after it diluted wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the side series of remedies from אביי's mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For heart weakness: roast ram's right thigh over cattle dung or willow twigs, eat it, then drink diluted wine.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: relish versus main food
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל. A לפתן needs enough to eat two meals of bread with it. A food that is not a לפתן needs enough to eat two meals of it. Raw meat counts as a food in its own right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Anything that is a relish must be enough to eat two meals with it. Anything that is not a relish must be enough to eat two meals of it. Raw meat must be enough to eat two meals of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic: how much food you need to make an עירוב. שמואל gives a general rule for measuring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to measure two meals' worth. A relish like a spread or dip is measured by how much bread it can accompany for two meals. A main food is measured by how much of that food itself makes two meals. Raw meat is placed in the second group, so you need enough raw meat itself for two meals.

keyTerms.meaning: relish; a food eaten together with bread
enough to eat with it (bread for two meals)
enough to eat of it (the food itself for two meals)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the small words בּוֹ (with it) and הֵימֶנּוּ (of it). They are the whole difference. With a relish, the bread is the meal. With a main food, the food itself is the meal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This two-category rule is the framework for the argument that follows about roasted meat.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא לִיפְתָּן, כְּדֵי לֶאֱכוֹל בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Anything that is a relish — enough to eat with it.
phrases.notes: That is, enough to go with the bread of two meals.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לִיפְתָּן, כְּדֵי לֶאֱכוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: Anything that is not a relish — enough to eat of it.
phrases.notes: That is, enough of the food itself for two meals.

phrases.english: Raw meat — enough to eat of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It leaves the medical side remarks and returns to the amounts of food for an עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A relish is measured by the bread it accompanies for two meals. A main food, including raw meat, is measured by two meals of the food itself.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף argue about roasted meat
steps.stepSummary: רבה says roasted meat is a relish, measured by the bread it accompanies. רב יוסף says it is a main food, measured by two meals of the meat itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Roasted meat: רבה says it must be enough to eat two meals with it. רב יוסף says it must be enough to eat two meals of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement about which of שמואל's two categories roasted meat belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that raw meat is a main food. The question is roasted meat. רבה sees it as something people eat with bread, so it is a relish. רב יוסף sees it as a food people eat on its own.

phrases.aramaic: בָּשָׂר צָלִי, רַבָּה אָמַר: כְּדֵי לֶאֱכוֹל בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Roasted meat — Rabba said: enough to eat with it,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: כְּדֵי לֶאֱכוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: and Rav Yosef said: enough to eat of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It applies שמואל's two categories to a case they disagree about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: רבה treats roasted meat as a relish, and רב יוסף treats it as a main food.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from the Persians
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף supports his view by pointing out that Persians eat roasted meat without bread. That shows roasted meat is a food in its own right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: From where do I say this? From the fact that these Persians eat pieces of roasted meat without bread!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a reason from real life for his position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a whole people eats roasted meat as a meal by itself, then roasted meat is not just a side dish for bread. So, he argues, it should be measured as a main food.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say this?; the speaker is about to give his source

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ —
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: From where do I say this?

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָנֵי פָּרְסָאֵי אָכְלִי טַבְהָקִי בְּלָא נַהֲמָא!
phrases.english: For these Persians eat pieces of roasted meat without bread!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף defends his side of the מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that roasted meat is a main food
steps.raayaSupportSource: The custom of the Persians to eat roasted meat without bread

steps.title: אביי: the Persians are not most of the world
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The Persians are not the majority of the world, and הלכה follows the normal practice of most people.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And are the Persians the majority of the world?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רב יוסף's proof with a short rhetorical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The habit of one group does not decide how a food is classified for everyone. Most of the world eats roasted meat with bread, so the Persian custom proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: the majority of the world; ordinary common practice
are they? (here part of a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And are the Persians the majority of the world?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects רב יוסף's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רב יוסף's position is not proven wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof relies on a minority custom, but halachic measures follow most people.

steps.title: Source: clothing of the poor and of the rich
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה. Small scraps of cloth count as a garment for the poor, while larger pieces are the standard for the rich. This shows that a group's special habits set the standard only for that group.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: Clothing of the poor counts for the poor; clothing of the rich counts for the rich.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a משנה to back up his point that a measure depends on what is normal, not on what an unusual group does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טומאה, a 3x3 fingerbreadth scrap counts as a garment for poor people, because they value small pieces. The general standard for everyone is 3x3 handbreadths. Likewise, the Persian custom may set a standard for Persians, but it does not change the general rule for the rest of the world.

keyTerms.meaning: clothing of the poor; small scraps of 3x3 fingerbreadths
clothing of the rich; pieces of 3x3 handbreadths

steps.whatToRemember: A halachic measure follows the normal practice of most people. An unusual group's habit sets a standard only for that group, not for everyone. That is why the Persians' custom cannot decide the status of roasted meat.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
clothing of the poor — for the poor,
phrases.notes: Small scraps of 3x3 fingerbreadths count as garments for poor people.

phrases.english: clothing of the rich — for the rich.
phrases.notes: The larger 3x3 handbreadth measure is the general standard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the textual support for אביי's rejection.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's principle that a minority custom does not set the general halachic standard
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about clothing of the poor and of the rich (כלים)
